transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-07 15:30 PDT
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Anand (Redwood SE), Mateo Cruz (Redwood SE), Mark Rivera (Sable CTO), Lina Okoye (Sable ML Eng), Tom Anders (Sable Head of Security), Sara Nguyen (Product)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be incomplete):
Sable MedTech is evaluating migrating from OpenAI-hosted endpoints to Redwood (considering hosted first, with Dedicated or Private later). Primary motivators: cost at scale, model compatibility with current vLLM/TGI stack, and audit/compliance needs (SOC2, VPC, KMS). They have an evaluation harness and want parity on generation quality and latency. Key asks: compatibility matrix for models, quantization/precision guidance, pilot cost estimate, and how Redwood handles KV/prefix cache and token accounting vs OpenAI.

Topics:
- Migration compatibility (OpenAI/Anthropic models -> Redwood)
- Performance parity, eval setup and metric mapping
- Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
- Security: VPC, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs, data residency
- Migration runbook and canary rollout suggestions

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intros? I'll pass to Priya after a 30 second overview of Redwood.
[00:12] Mark: Hi all, Mark here, CTO at Sable. We run clinical summarization and an internal assistant. Lina and Tom with me.
[00:18] Lina: Hi. We're primarily using vLLM in house with TGI for some models and OpenAI for prod right now. Trying to get costs down and get more control.
[00:26] Tom: Security chief, just here to ask the hard questions later.
[00:29] Jordan: Great. Redwood is a serving platform for inference — hosted API for fast start, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private for VPC/on-prem. Priya will go deeper into migration scenarios.
[00:40] Priya: Thanks. Quick check: you mentioned vLLM and TGI — are you currently running a custom LLM stack for dev and OpenAI in prod?
[00:48] Lina: Exactly. Dev runs vLLM on prem and uses TGI for some fine-tuned variants. Prod calls OpenAI for assistant responses. Costs spiked as we scaled token volumes.
[00:59] Priya: Understood. Main migration patterns we see: 1) lift-and-shift to Redwood Hosted — swap model endpoints if the model artifacts are supported, 2) Dedicated fleet for predictable throughput, 3) Private for isolated networks and strict compliance. Any must-have for go/no-go?
[01:12] Mark: Two things: eval parity with our current OpenAI outputs and security/compliance. Also latency SLO — under 300ms p50 for short prompts, and cost target per 1k tokens.
[01:24] Sara: Product also cares about hallucination regressions — we have a test suite.
[01:27] Priya: Perfect. On compatibility: many OpenAI/Anthropic model families have equivalent checkpoints we support; for community models we often recommend particular quantization profiles (eg --ql4x vs q8) and we provide a compatibility matrix. We'll share specifics.
[01:42] Lina: How exact is the parity? We've got prompts that are very sensitive to minor tokenization differences. vLLM sometimes uses different tokenization than API variants.
[01:50] Mateo: Good point — tokenization differences come up. We attempt to match tokenizer and model weights; for API-only models sometimes we use Redmonk (?) — sorry, the autogenerated name went weird — we map to the nearest model and run evals to confirm parity.
[02:04] Mark: Can you run our eval harness or do we need to adapt it?
[02:08] Priya: We can ingest your eval suite. Usually customers share their CSV of prompts and expected outputs; we run a parity and regression report comparing generations, BLEU/ROUGE-ish metrics, and embedding similarity. We'll flag deterministic mismatch due to sampling/temperature differences.
[02:24] Tom: On the security side: SOC2 is a must, plus SAML/SSO, KMS integration for key management, and audit logs preserved for 1 year. Also, data residency in us-east.
[02:35] Jordan: We will send our SOC2 report and security pack. Redwood supports SAML, KMS integrations, and can route Dedicated clusters into your VPC if you go Private. Audit logs are configurable; retention is an add-on but we can provide a baseline.
[02:50] Tom: For Private, how much operational overhead? We can't be full-time ops on it.
[02:55] Priya: Private has a customer-managed network with a Redwood control plane. We provide an on-prem package option and can run hybrid with a managed operator. For low ops teams we recommend Dedicated as a middle ground: predictable capacity, SLAs, and less hands-on.
[03:12] Lina: On inference behavior — how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? That matters for our clinical conversation use case.
[03:18] Mateo: Our runtime supports KV cache handling and automatic prefix caching policies. We have documented best practices — when you move from an API-based provider we often see improvements in per-token latency with continuous batching and cache-friendly request routing. We'll include a note about warm vs cold cache effects for your use patterns.
[03:38] Lina: Batching is good, but we need p95 latency guarantees for interactive use. Will batching impact that?
[03:44] Priya: We have hybrid batching that respects latency SLOs; there's an autoscaler for Dedicated. For Hosted we offer latency tiers and can pin requests to lower-concurrency paths for low-latency routes. That's part of the cost/latency tradeoff we can model.
[03:59] Mark: Cost model — we currently pay X per 1M tokens on OpenAI and run about 800M tokens/mo across embeddings and chat. What ballpark can you provide?
[04:10] Jordan: We'll need to run numbers but typical savings come from quantized models on Dedicated and caching for repeated prefixes. For example, customers running Llama-2-13B quantized to q4x on Dedicated often see 30-60% token-cost reduction compared to non-quantized API calls. We'll prepare a side-by-side.
[04:28] Lina: What about vLLM compatibility? We sometimes have specialized attention kernels.
[04:33] Mateo: We try to match model architecture and provide kernel selection; for certain custom kernels we may need to validate with your infra. Also, GPU and GPU driver versions can impact latency; we will include a hardware compatibility checklist.
[04:48] [Speaker 1 — low volume, overlap] Tom: (mumbles) encryption at rest for model shards?
[04:52] Priya: Yes, for Private we support encrypted model storage and integration with customer KMS/HSM. For Dedicated we offer disk encryption and customer-managed keys under certain contracts.
[05:02] Mark: We have a small concern with regenerations and token accounting differences between services. How do you report tokens and costs?
[05:08] Jordan: Redwood reports token-level breakdowns per request and per model; our console shows total input and output tokens, cost estimates, and you can export granular logs. We'll include a sample CSV.
[05:20] Sara: If we do a pilot, what's a minimal pilot footprint? We want to test parity and cost on our top 50 prompts.
[05:28] Priya: A typical pilot is 2–4 weeks, 1–2 dedicated GPUs for throughput parity, plus a hosted fallback. We'll scope based on your traffic profile. For parity we run deterministic seeds where possible and sampling comparisons.
[05:40] Lina: How do you handle model updates/rollouts? We need canary and automatic fallback to OpenAI for regressions.
[05:47] Mateo: Rollouts are supported — canary percentages, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. You can pin versions per route and set rollback triggers based on eval metrics or error rates.
[05:58] Mark: About evals — you mentioned embedding similarity for responses. We use embedding-based reranking; any differences in embedding model between providers can change rerank results.
[06:08] Priya: We recommend freezing embedding model versions and provide embeddings parity tests. If you need exact parity with OpenAI embeddings, we’ll discuss nearest equivalent or proxy model and show similarity scores.
[06:20] Tom: If we move to Dedicated, will Redwood handle SOC2 audits or do we?
[06:26] Jordan: Redwood's Hosted and Dedicated services are covered under our SOC2 for the control plane and managed services; for Private you own more controls. We'll provide specifics in the security pack.
[06:36] Mark: Can you run a short benchmark with our top 50 prompts on q4x and q8 quant profiles and share latency percentiles?
[06:43] Priya: Yes — please share the CSV and token distribution. We'll do runs on hosted and Dedicated configs and give p50/p95 numbers plus cost per 1k tokens.
[06:53] Lina: A note — some prompts include PHI; we need data handling assurances.
[06:57] Tom: Right, PHI handling, retention policies, and audit logs for accesses.
[07:03] Jordan: We'll mark PHI as a redline and route you to enterprise security for contractual language; also discuss possible on-prem Private options.
[07:10] Sara: Timeline wise, we're hoping to make a decision in 6 weeks and run a pilot in Q3.
[07:15] Jordan: Sounds good. We'll prioritize sending the security pack and a pricing model this week.
[07:20] [00:07:25] (roughly) 
[07:25] Priya: Quick technical aside — if you rely on vLLM attention tweaks, we can validate kernel parity but might ask for a short dev env access or a reproducible test.
[07:34] Mark: We can set up a limited dev endpoint.
[07:37] Lina: One more question: do you support streaming with structured tool-calls? Our assistant does tools and function outputs.
[07:44] Mateo: Yes, streaming with function/tool-calls is supported on Hosted and Dedicated. Private supports the same plumbing; you just host the connectors.
[07:52] Tom: Any known gotchas migrating from TGI? We sometimes use custom stop sequences and soft prompts.
[07:58] Priya: Stop sequences are standard but soft prompts/hard-coded prefix tricks sometimes need adaptation; we can help translate those to Redwood routing/templating.
[08:10] Mark: Ok let's summarize next steps.
[08:13] Jordan: Recap: 1) Sable to share CSV of top 50–100 eval prompts and token distribution (Lina). 2) Redwood (Priya) to run parity runs on Hosted + Dedicated and share latency/cost and quantized profiles. 3) Jordan to send SOC2/security pack and link to console export sample. 4) Schedule technical deep-dive for next week with infra folks.
[08:30] Sara: Confirming TL;DR: pilot -> parity -> cost model -> decision in ~6 weeks.
[08:34] Tom: I'll send the security requirement doc and PHI checklist to Jordan.
[08:38] Jordan: Great. Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and the files.

End transcript.
